page.overview:
Who is Chirostenotes?

(meaning "narrow-handed") is an extinct genus of oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in Alberta, Canada during the Late Cretaceous period. It was a small, quick hunter with long slender hands. Since its discovery, Chirostenotes has been put into several different branches of the dinosaur family tree - including the oviraptorid and dromaeosaur families. Currently, it is a part of the caenagnathid family, but that may change once more fossils are uncovered.

This little dinosaur has been the subject of a good amount of study over the years. There were once four species named, but are now separated into their own genus or are synonyms. As a later Cretaceous member of the maniraptorid, it may have been a feathered dinosaur based on current thinking about this family.

Chirostenotes was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its artwork, it is shown chasing a lizard.

Chirostenotes also appeared in the Dinosaur Field Guide, but in the Jurassic World Dinosaur Field Guide it was completely replaced by Anzu.
